# S100 — Clarify when to start a slice in agent workflows

Agent guidance presents `next --start --show` as a one-call option while also requiring agents to inspect the slice and resolve ambiguity before starting work. State one clear sequence so efficiency guidance does not encourage premature status changes.

**Findings:** AI credit-flow review · **Size: S** · **Tree:** docs

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

The current examples can leave agents unsure whether they should mark work started before validating its scope and acceptance criteria.

## Files

- `src/slicer/ai.py`
- `docs/agents.md`
- `tests/test_ai.py` or focused documentation checks

## Failing tests

1. A focused assertion or review check confirms the standard flow reads the slice before marking it started.
2. Any documented `next --start` shortcut clearly identifies when it is appropriate and does not conflict with the spec-first flow.

## Implement

Choose and document a single default sequence: fetch the next item and slice, inspect scope/dependencies/checks, resolve ambiguity, then start. Retain the combined start shortcut only with a clear precondition that the specification is already trusted. Keep descriptions consistent across quick start and detailed reference.

## Check

The quick start, reusable prompt, and detailed reference agree on when status changes, and a new agent can follow the workflow without choosing between contradictory examples.
